instrument
label: Instrument
description: A wind chime of tubes hanging from a disc, or a glockenspiel of bars on a frame

name: scale
label: Scale
description: The notes, from the lowest up: a scale or a chord. Westminster is the Big Ben quarters (lowest note B for the original key)

name: root
label: Lowest note
description: The note of the longest tube or bar

name: octave
label: Octave
description: Octave of the lowest note (C4 is middle C, A4 = 440 Hz); the range keeps every tube or bar between the shortest that can be drilled and the longest that can be handled

name: N
label: Notes
description: How many tubes or bars, following the scale up; at most two octaves

name: tubeMat
label: Tube material
description: Young's modulus, density and shear modulus of the tube

name: tubeSize
label: Tube size
description: Outside diameter x wall in mm

name: strikeGap
label: Striker gap
description: Gap between the striker and the tubes at rest

name: barMat
label: Bar material
description: Young's modulus along the bar, density and shear modulus. Wood bars are straight (not undercut): a starting point, tune by ear

name: barT
label: Bar thickness
description: Thickness of the bars (they bend through it)

title: Tuned chimes
description: A wind chime of tubes, or a glockenspiel of bars, that is in tune before you cut it: pick the scale, the lowest note, the number of notes, the material and the tube or bar size; every tube or bar gets the length of its note from the free-free beam (Euler-Bernoulli with the Timoshenko correction) and its cord or pin holes at the nodes, 0.2242 L from each end. Variables f1..f12 are the frequencies (Hz) and L1..L12 the cut lengths; assert.list proves each length and hole. Metal is within about a quarter semitone, wood is a starting point: cut long, then tune with a tuner. Export the face set "Cut sheet" as SVG for the disc and sail (or the frame).
